1.title: Course Introduction and Exam Orientation
1.text: Welcome to Module zero: Course Introduction and Exam Orientation. This module covers exam orientation and the course map. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. What the exam is: sixty items, one hundred twenty minutes, a scaled score of seven hundred twenty to pass. The seven domains, their weights and the thirty objectives behind them. The minimally qualified candidate the exam is written for. The decision rules that explain most correct answers. How the course is built and how to use it.

1.title: Case Check-In: Cedarbrook Outfitters
1.text: Our running case is Cedarbrook Outfitters. Cedarbrook Outfitters. Throughout the course you follow Cedarbrook Outfitters, a fictional outdoor-gear retailer. Its operations, marketing and customer-care teams adopt Claude for reports, campaign copy, reply drafts and planning. Each module solves one problem the teams meet; the questions use the same style as the exam.

1.title: The Exam at a Glance
1.text: The Exam at a Glance. The figure shows this: The C C A O F exam at a glance: sixty items, one hundred twenty minutes, scaled score one hundred to one thousand with seven hundred twenty to pass, seven domains, U S D ninety-nine, valid twelve months.

1.title: The Exam at a Glance, continued
1.text: The Exam at a Glance, continued. Credential or code. Claude Associate to Foundations or C C A O F. Items. sixty, multiple choice and multiple response; each item says how many answers to select. Time. one hundred twenty minutes (two minutes per item). Passing score. seven hundred twenty on a scaled range of one hundred to one thousand (criterion-referenced: a fixed standard, not a ranking). Fee. U S D ninety-nine per attempt. Delivery. Proctored by Pearson V U E: online or at a test center. Validity. twelve months from the date the credential is awarded; on-time renewal is a free, non-proctored assessment.

1.title: The Exam at a Glance, continued
1.text: The Exam at a Glance, continued. Retakes. Wait fourteen days after the first failed attempt, thirty after the second, ninety after the third; at most four attempts in a rolling twelve months; limits are per exam. Prerequisites. None are required; regular hands-on use of Claude is recommended; no software or A P I (application programming interface) experience is needed. Score report. Pass or fail, the scaled score, and the percent correct per domain (domain figures do not decide pass or fail). Exam tip: For a multiple-response item the stem says how many answers to select: read that number first, then choose exactly that many.

1.title: The Seven Domains
1.text: The Seven Domains. The figure shows this: Domain weights: D two Output Evaluation and Validation twenty-one, D four Workflow Integration and Solution Design sixteen, D six Governance, Risk and Responsible Use fifteen, D one Prompting and Task Execution fourteen, D three Product and Model Selection twelve, D five Configuration and Knowledge Management twelve, D seven Troubleshooting and Optimization ten.

1.title: The Seven Domains, continued
1.text: The Seven Domains, continued. D two Output Evaluation and Validation. Weight: twenty-one percent. What it asks you to do: Check accuracy and completeness; spot hallucinations, inconsistencies and bias; fact-check; know when a human must review; edit and adapt; choose output formats. Modules: three to five. D four Workflow Integration and Solution Design. Weight: sixteen percent. What it asks you to do: Analyze requirements; research and plan; support design; fit Claude into workflows; explain value and limits. Modules: nine, ten. D six Governance, Risk, and Responsible Use. Weight: fifteen percent. What it asks you to do: Appropriate and inappropriate uses; data sensitivity and privacy; organizational policy; ethics. Modules: thirteen, fourteen.

1.title: The Seven Domains, continued
1.text: The Seven Domains, continued. D one Prompting and Task Execution. Weight: fourteen percent. What it asks you to do: Write effective prompts; decompose tasks; iterate; adapt to the task type. Modules: one, two. D three Product and Model Selection. Weight: twelve percent. What it asks you to do: Choose features; tell Haiku, Sonnet and Opus apart; manage context and memory. Modules: six to eight. D five Configuration and Knowledge Management. Weight: twelve percent. What it asks you to do: Configure Projects; manage knowledge and connectors; write system-level instructions; keep them current. Modules: eleven, twelve. D seven Troubleshooting and Optimization. Weight: ten percent. What it asks you to do: Diagnose weak prompts and poor outputs; adjust on feedback; optimize workflows. Modules: fifteen, sixteen.

1.title: The Seven Domains, continued
1.text: The Seven Domains, continued. Of sixty items, about thirteen come from D two, ten from D four, nine from D six, eight from D one, seven each from D three and D five, and six from D seven. Weights are the approximate share of scored items. Items are written against the thirty objectives listed in the guide. Study order by value: D two first, then D four, D six and D one. Every domain is at least ten percent, so none can be skipped. Exam tip: No domain is small. The weakest domain on your practice results is the cheapest place to gain points.

1.title: The Minimally Qualified Candidate
1.text: The Minimally Qualified Candidate. The minimally qualified candidate (M Q C) can. turn a business goal into a clear, structured prompt, and break big requests into steps. check Claude's output for accuracy, completeness and bias before anyone relies on it. choose the right feature (chat, search, Research, Projects, Artifacts) and the right model for the job. configure a Project with instructions and knowledge, and connect tools such as Google Drive. protect sensitive data and follow the organization's A I policy. fix weak outputs and tune workflows. recognize limits and escalate technical work to Developers and Architects.

1.title: The Minimally Qualified Candidate, continued
1.text: The Minimally Qualified Candidate, continued. The figure shows this: The minimally qualified candidate prompts, evaluates, selects, integrates, configures, governs and troubleshoots Claude in everyday work.

1.title: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward
1.text: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward. Most items describe a business situation and ask for the best action. The best answer usually follows one of these rules. Each later module shows them at work.

1.title: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued
1.text: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued. one. Rule: Verify facts, numbers and citations against an authoritative source before sharing. Typical wrong answers: "Claude sounded confident", "ask Claude to rate itself". two. Rule: Be specific: goal, audience, context, format and constraints in the prompt. Typical wrong answers: A vague one-line request, or "just retry". three. Rule: Break complex work into steps and review each. Typical wrong answers: One giant prompt with no review. four. Rule: Match the model and effort to the task: lighter for routine and high-volume, stronger for hard reasoning. Typical wrong answers: "Always the biggest model", "never use Research".

1.title: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued
1.text: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued. five. Rule: Use the lightest feature that fits: chat for quick, web search for current facts, Research for deep reports. Typical wrong answers: Research for a one-line fact. six. Rule: Put standing context in a Project (instructions and knowledge), not in every prompt. Typical wrong answers: Pasting the same background each time. seven. Rule: Protect sensitive data: remove or anonymize identifiers; follow policy; use approved tools. Typical wrong answers: "Tell Claude not to retain it", uploading as-is. eight. Rule: Keep a qualified human in the loop for high-stakes or regulated decisions. Typical wrong answers: Letting Claude decide alone.

1.title: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued
1.text: Ten Decision Rules the Questions Reward, continued. nine. Rule: Start a fresh chat or summarize when a conversation gets long or drifts. Typical wrong answers: Piling on more messages. ten. Rule: Escalate technical, integration or architecture work to Developers or Architects. Typical wrong answers: Improvising an A P I integration. Exam tip: When two options both work, prefer the one that verifies, protects data, fits the task and keeps a person accountable.

1.title: How to Use This Course
1.text: How to Use This Course. Order: read modules one to sixteen in order (they follow the domains), then module seventeen (recap) and eighteen (technique). Each module has the objectives it covers, a case, tables, figures, Exam tips, scenario questions with explanations and a Quick Reference Card. Practice on the real product. The guide recommends building a Project with instructions and knowledge and evaluating outputs for accuracy and bias. Do the small exercises as you read.

1.title: How to Use This Course, continued
1.text: How to Use This Course, continued. Product details change fast. Boxes marked show current behavior (plan limits, menu names, model lineup). On the exam, answer by the principle and check the Help Center for current details. Independence. 1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Exam: C C A O F; sixty items; one hundred twenty min; pass seven hundred twenty of one thousand; U S D ninety-nine; valid twelve months. Domains: D two twenty-one, D four sixteen, D six fifteen, D one fourteen, D three twelve, D five twelve, D seven ten. Objectives: thirty in all. Prerequisites: None required; hands-on Claude use recommended; no A P I skills needed. Retakes: fourteen, thirty, ninety days; max four per rolling twelve months. Ten rules: Verify, be specific, decompose, match model and effort, lightest feature, Project for standing context, protect data, human in the loop, restart or summarize, escalate. In the next module, we continue the course.
